brief: Goldman's Garrett reads the week's selloff as the market finally pricing vol it had refused to: the 6-week straddle flagged the prior weekend realized 2x, and its price doubled from 4% to 8.2%, with convexity at panic levels last seen in 2025 Liberation Day, 2020 COVID, and the 2022 Fed hiking cycle. He names it an 'AI conviction crisis': the trade isn't abandoned, but capital intensity, financing, ROI, and valuations are questioned together. Professional investors had already cut net exposure to 1-year lows with no long-delta buying, yet breadth held up and damage stayed concentrated in prior high-conviction names, with top-decile 1H26 stocks down 32% since July. He argues volume and implied vol spiking together historically signals a crescendo rather than a continuation, and that the vol-implied breakeven matching equities' long-run annualized return makes much higher vol hard without something breaking. He recommends long-delta, short-vol or vega-flat structures and, with Ben Snider, calls hyperscalers the best vol-adjusted trade regardless of which AI capex payback scenario plays out. Desk notes add: hedge funds and CTAs are heavily net short and washed out, liquidity is thin, the panic index reads 9.8 of 10, and cyclicals-versus-AI performance echoes the 2018 drawdown.
